payload.fact: Domtar had 450 AI-assisted sensors, yet a motor failed; its reliability engineer estimated that one day of vibration data would take 32 weeks to analyze.
payload.expected: Hundreds of predictive-maintenance sensors would make equipment failures easier to prevent.
payload.actual: The sensors produced a review queue far beyond one engineer's capacity until Domtar changed its support routine.
payload.tension: The monitoring capability created more information than the operating process could use.
payload.target: The deployment decision that treated instrumentation as a complete maintenance system.
payload.reader_realization: More detection did not help until Domtar staffed a routine for interpreting and acting on it.

angles.line: A motor failure looked less alarming because Domtar had 450 AI sensors, until one day of their data turned into 32 weeks of review.
The impressive sensor network was constrained by one engineer facing an impossible review queue.
More maintenance data produced less usable monitoring because nobody could review it in time.
Installing more sensors became a plan for preventing failures without a plan for reading what they produced.
The sensor deployment looked like a maintenance system until the missing analyst routine became visible.
